summary_oneline: Add a `navauth self upgrade` CLI that applies navigator-auth's SQL migrations with admin credentials, replacing three silent startup runners and hand-applied patches.

localization.role: identity runner: applies 001-006 to auth.user_identities, collects failures, raises once
hand-maintained ordered registry of identity SQL files (a file not listed is inert)
per-file executor, duplicated verbatim in all three runners; ignores the result of conn.execute()
vault runner: 2 files, stops at first failure, no schema templating
only runner that substitutes {schema} / {users_table} from conf
passkey runner, executed only when the passkey backend is enabled
startup hook that runs vault + identity migrations on the runtime pool app['authdb']
log-only startup wrapper for the vault runner
log-only startup wrapper for the identity runner
passkey startup hook; raises ConfigError when the migration fails
the single runtime DB credential set (DBUSER/DBPWD/...); no admin credential setting exists
configurable schema / table names that migration SQL should honour
hand-applied auth.clients patch that no runner loads — the manual workflow the source describes
packaging scope (navigator_auth* only); where a first [project.scripts] entry would be added
existing runner tests (mocked pool, SQL-text assertions) that import SQL_DIR from the runner module
pending FEAT-106 task that will add a fourth runner (MFA) and documents the execute() never-raises contract

constraints.statement: asyncdb's conn.execute() never raises; it returns [None, <error>] and the existing `_run_sql` copies ignore that value
constraints.implication: the new command must use a fail-closed execution path (check the result or use a raising call) and verify the outcome, otherwise 'applied' is unreliable

constraints.statement: Every existing SQL file is idempotent by construction (IF NOT EXISTS + catalog-guarded DO blocks) and is designed to be re-run
constraints.implication: new files under the migrations folder must keep that style; re-running everything is safe, so a ledger adds reporting rather than correctness

constraints.statement: Only `navigator_auth*` is packaged in `pyproject.toml`; a repo-root docs/ folder is outside the wheel
constraints.implication: an installed `navauth` cannot read docs/migrations/ unless the SQL also ships inside the package

constraints.statement: Two SQL conventions coexist: identity/vault hard-code `auth.`, passkey (and the planned MFA file) use {schema}/{users_table} rendered by `render_sql`
constraints.implication: a single runner needs one rendering rule that leaves hard-coded files untouched

constraints.statement: Existing tests import `SQL_DIR` and the file tuples from `navigator_auth/identity/migrations.py`, `navigator_auth/vault/migrations.py` and `navigator_auth/passkey/migrations.py`
constraints.implication: moving SQL files or removing `ensure_identity_columns` / `ensure_vault_tables` / `ensure_passkey_tables` breaks tests unless shims are kept
admin credentials need a new input (flag, env var or setting); the DSN must never be printed

constraints.statement: Base tables of the auth schema are created by the Navigator platform, not by this library
constraints.implication: the command applies additive changes on top of an existing schema; it does not bootstrap a database

constraints.statement: TASK-130 (FEAT-106, pending) will add an MFA runner in the per-subsystem style
constraints.implication: the two features must agree on where MFA SQL lives and who runs it, or the new command lands already incomplete

constraints.statement: No console script, argparse, click or typer usage exists in the package or its history
constraints.implication: `navauth` is the first CLI; the navigator-vault design in TASK-076 (other repo) is the only precedent

new: Console script `navauth` (first `[project.scripts]` entry) with a `self upgrade` subcommand; async entry via asyncio.run, `main(argv) -> int`, explicit exit codes
One central migration runner that discovers ordered SQL files, renders {schema}/{users_table}, executes fail-closed and reports per-file status
A `self upgrade --check` / dry-run mode that reports pending work without changing the database
`docs/migrations/` folder (SQL-based changes plus a README explaining how to add one)
An admin-credential input for DDL (e.g. `--dsn`, then an env var, then navconfig), separate from the runtime DBUSER
Migration files for changes that are manual today (the auth.clients patch)

modified.change: add `[project.scripts] navauth = ...`; ensure SQL files ship as package data
`ensure_identity_columns` delegates to the central runner; `_MIGRATION_FILES` registry replaced by discovery
`ensure_passkey_tables` delegates; `render_sql` becomes the shared rendering rule
`auth_startup` behaviour for migrations (keep, check-only, or remove) per the answer to U3
converted into a numbered migration and retired as a loose patch (if in scope, U4)

untouched: Creation of the base auth schema and tables (owned by the Navigator platform)
Data migrations and vault key rotation (the `navigator-vault` CLI in navigator-session)
The content of already-released SQL files (001-006 identity, vault 001-002, passkey 001)

patterns.pattern: Idempotent SQL: header comment with FEAT id, `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, DO blocks guarded on to_regclass / catalog lookups
Collect failures, keep running later files, raise once naming every failed file
CLI shape from the navigator-vault precedent: DSN from `--dsn` then env then navconfig, injectable factories, explicit exit codes, DSN never printed
Fail-closed execution with a `to_regclass` / fetchval confirmation, as TASK-130 specifies for MFA
Runner tests with a mocked pool plus SQL-text assertions

risks.risk: Silent success: execute() swallows errors, so the command could report 'upgraded' on a failed file
risks.mitigation: inspect the result / use a raising call and verify with catalog probes

risks.risk: docs/migrations/ is not in the wheel, so the command works only from a checkout
risks.mitigation: keep the SQL inside the package and expose docs/migrations/ as the documented view (U1)

risks.risk: Collision with FEAT-106 TASK-130, which adds a fourth per-subsystem runner
risks.mitigation: sequence the two features or have TASK-130 target the central runner

risks.risk: Removing startup migrations breaks deployments that rely on them
risks.mitigation: keep the startup call as a shim or a check-only warning for one release (U3)

risks.risk: Applying optional-feature tables (passkey, MFA) to databases that do not use them
risks.mitigation: explicit selection rule or documented 'apply all' decision (U4)

risks.risk: 006 removes a legacy column; running it with elevated credentials on an unexpected schema is destructive
risks.mitigation: keep its catalog guards, offer `--check`, never weaken the guard

confidence_map.statement: Three independent migration runners exist (identity 6 files, vault 2, passkey 1), each with its own sql/ folder and a duplicated `_run_sql`
Vault and identity migrations already run automatically at every app startup through `auth_startup`, with the runtime pool, and failures are only logged
confidence_map.reasoning: Direct read of auth.py:178-192 and the wrappers. This contradicts the source's premise that every change is applied by hand.

confidence_map.statement: The local auth.user_identities lag is most likely a startup migration that failed silently (insufficient DDL rights, lock timeout, or an error swallowed by execute())
confidence_map.reasoning: Inferred from several findings; the local database was not inspected.

confidence_map.statement: No applied-migrations ledger table exists; correctness rests on idempotent SQL
confidence_map.reasoning: Negative grep over navigator_auth/, docs/, documentation/ plus runner comments.

confidence_map.statement: navigator-auth has no CLI and never had a console script; `navauth` would be the first
confidence_map.reasoning: Negative grep plus pickaxe over full git history.

confidence_map.statement: There is no admin/DDL credential setting; only DBUSER/DBPWD via `default_dsn`
`navigator_auth/backends/oauth2/ddl.sql` is a hand-applied patch referenced by no Python code
confidence_map.reasoning: Grep found no loader; a dynamic loader outside the searched paths cannot be fully excluded.

confidence_map.statement: A repo-root docs/migrations/ folder would not be available to a pip-installed navauth
confidence_map.reasoning: packages.find includes only navigator_auth*; whether in-package *.sql currently ships as package data was not verified against a built wheel.

confidence_map.statement: asyncdb conn.execute() never raises, so the current runners can report success without applying anything
confidence_map.reasoning: Recorded as verified in TASK-130 and in session memory; not re-run in this research.

confidence_map.statement: A hand-maintained file registry has already caused an inert migration (006 added but not registered)
The navigator-vault CLI (TASK-076) is a usable design precedent for DSN resolution and exit codes, but its code lives in another repository
confidence_map.reasoning: Task document only; the sibling repo was not read.

confidence_map.statement: FEAT-106 TASK-130 will add a fourth runner in the same per-subsystem style
confidence_map.reasoning: Active task document read via wiki.

confidence_map.statement: A central runner plus thin `ensure_*` shims can satisfy the request without rewriting released SQL
confidence_map.reasoning: Design inference from the identical runner shapes; depends on the answers to U1-U4.

unknowns.question: Where should the SQL files physically live, given that docs/ is not packaged in the wheel?
plausible_answers: inside the package (navigator_auth/migrations/), with docs/migrations/ holding the README/index
docs/migrations/ only, command works from a source checkout
docs/migrations/ as source of truth, copied into the package at build time
unknowns.user_answer: In package + docs index: SQL lives inside the package (e.g. navigator_auth/migrations/) so an installed navauth always finds it; docs/migrations/ holds the README and index of changes.

unknowns.question: How should `self upgrade` decide what is pending?
plausible_answers: ledger table recording applied files + checksum
no ledger: re-run every idempotent file and verify via catalog probes
ledger for reporting plus idempotent re-run for safety
unknowns.user_answer: Ledger + idempotent SQL: a small table records each applied file with checksum and timestamp; files stay idempotent as a safety net.

unknowns.question: Once the command exists, what should app startup do about migrations?
plausible_answers: keep applying at startup (command is an extra path)
startup only checks and warns; DDL only via the command
unknowns.user_answer: Check and warn only: startup no longer runs DDL; it detects pending migrations and logs a warning telling the operator to run navauth self upgrade.

unknowns.question: Which change sets does the first version cover?
plausible_answers: all existing sets including optional passkey/MFA
all existing sets plus the manual auth.clients patch
unknowns.user_answer: Everything incl. auth.clients: identity, vault, passkey and the manual auth.clients patch converted to a migration; MFA joins when FEAT-106 lands.

recommended_next_command.rationale: Localization is verified and the four design forks are user decisions captured as unknowns; once answered there is a single architecture (central runner + CLI + shims) to specify.

meta.notes: Admin-credential input is not asked as an unknown: the navigator-vault precedent (--dsn, then env var, then navconfig) is taken as the default and left for the spec. Follow-up worth running at spec time: build a wheel and confirm whether in-package *.sql files are included; inspect the local database to confirm C3.
